claims.support: Standard photodetector theory; the report gives no source. The relation actually used is the RESPONSIVITY relation, not a QE relation: R [A/W] = eta * lambda[um] / 1.24. Verified readable source: Hamamatsu Photonics, 'Si photodiodes' Technical note, Cat. No. KSPD9001E04, Dec 2025, section 2-3 'Spectral response', printed p.6, equation (2-3): QE = [S x 1240 / lambda] x 100 [%] (S in A/W, lambda in nm); the same page has Figure 2-8 'Spectral response (Si photodiodes)' with a dashed QE=100% reference line (plot labels read, individual curve points not extracted).
claims.correction: Cite either: Hamamatsu Photonics K.K., 'Si photodiodes', Technical note KSPD9001E04, Dec. 2025, sec. 2-3, eq. (2-3); or RP Photonics Encyclopedia, 'Responsivity', DOI 10.61835/xal (R = eta.e/(h.nu); worked example 90% QE at 800 nm -> 0.58 A/W). ALSO REWORD: QE itself is not proportional to lambda; it is the responsivity (and the falling photon energy) that makes the Si response rise from ~550 nm toward ~800-900 nm.

claims.support: [3] abstract read verbatim (PubMed PMID 7873641): 'synthesis and properties'; it advertises no model, no HOMO-LUMO arithmetic, no chain-length theory - and its own wavelengths are Cy3 546 nm / Cy5 633-647 nm, not 550/649 nm. Arithmetic (computed here, hc=1239.842 eV.nm): 550->649 nm = 0.344 eV; 570->670 nm = 0.325 eV; 649-550 = 99 nm. So '~0.33 eV' is right to about +/-0.02 eV and '~100 nm' is correct - but 100 nm/vinylene is empirical, not a prediction of Kuhn's box model (lambda ~ L^2/(N+1)).
